question: According to the Maine CDL manual, how far can the danger zone extend from the front bumper of a school bus?
choice_b: 10 feet
choice_c: 50 feet
choice_d: 20 feet
explanation: The danger zone may extend as much as 30 feet from the front bumper of the bus, with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.1.1 Danger Zones

question: Which side of a school bus is always considered dangerous, according to the manual, because of passing cars?
choice_b: The right side
choice_c: The roof area
choice_d: The left side
explanation: The manual states the area to the left of the bus is always considered dangerous because of passing cars.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.1.1 Danger Zones

question: Where are the outside left and right side flat mirrors mounted on a school bus?
choice_a: Inside the bus above the windshield
choice_b: On the rear bumper
choice_c: At the left and right front corners of the bus, at the side or front of the windshield
choice_d: On the roof at the rear of the bus
explanation: The outside flat mirrors are mounted at the left and right front corners of the bus at the side or front of the windshield and are used to monitor traffic, clearances, and students at the sides and rear.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.1.3 Outside Left and Right Side Flat Mirrors

question: When properly adjusted, the outside flat mirrors should let the driver see how far behind the bus?
choice_b: 100 feet or 2 bus lengths
choice_c: 400 feet or 8 bus lengths
choice_d: 200 feet or 4 bus lengths
explanation: The flat mirrors should be adjusted so the driver can see 200 feet, or 4 bus lengths, behind the bus, along the sides of the bus, and the rear tires touching the ground.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.1.3 Outside Left and Right Side Flat Mirrors

question: The blind spot directly behind a school bus, not covered by the outside flat mirrors, can extend up to how many feet depending on the bus's length and width?
choice_b: 200 feet
choice_c: 400 feet
choice_d: 100 feet
explanation: The manual states the blind spot behind the bus extends 50 to 150 feet and could extend up to 400 feet depending on the length and width of the bus.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.1.3 Outside Left and Right Side Flat Mirrors

question: Where are the outside left and right side convex mirrors located on a school bus?
choice_b: Inside the cab only
choice_c: Above the outside flat mirrors
choice_d: Below the outside flat mirrors
explanation: The convex mirrors are located below the outside flat mirrors and are used to monitor the left and right sides of the bus at a wide angle.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.1.4 Outside Left and Right Side Convex Mirrors

question: What is true about the image a school bus driver sees in the convex mirrors?
choice_a: It shows people and objects at their true size and distance
choice_b: It magnifies distant objects for a clearer view
choice_c: It shows the interior of the bus only
choice_d: It does not accurately reflect the true size and distance of people or objects
explanation: The manual notes that convex mirrors present a view of people and objects that does not accurately reflect their size and distance from the bus.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.1.4 Outside Left and Right Side Convex Mirrors

question: When properly positioned, the convex mirrors should let the driver see at least how much of the adjacent lanes?
choice_a: Half a traffic lane on the right side only
choice_b: One traffic lane on either side of the bus
choice_c: The convex mirrors are not intended to show traffic lanes
choice_d: Two full traffic lanes on either side
explanation: The convex mirrors should be positioned to show the entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts, the front of the rear tires touching the ground, and at least one traffic lane on either side of the bus.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.1.4 Outside Left and Right Side Convex Mirrors

question: What is the main purpose of the outside left and right side crossover mirrors on a school bus?
choice_a: To check tire pressure without stopping
choice_b: To monitor passenger activity inside the bus
choice_c: To see the front bumper danger zone area directly in front of the bus that is not visible by direct vision
choice_d: To see 400 feet behind the bus
explanation: Crossover mirrors are used to see the front bumper danger zone directly in front of the bus, which is not visible by direct vision, as well as the danger zones to the left and right sides.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.1.5 Outside Left and Right Side Crossover Mirrors

question: According to the manual, what should overlap when the crossover mirrors are correctly adjusted?
choice_a: The convex mirror image and the overhead mirror image
choice_b: The interior dome light and the exterior lights
choice_c: Direct vision and mirror view vision
choice_d: The stop arm and the flashing red lights
explanation: Crossover mirrors should be adjusted so the entire area in front of the bus, from the bumper to the point where direct vision is possible, is covered, and direct vision and mirror view vision should overlap.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.1.5 Outside Left and Right Side Crossover Mirrors

question: The large blind spot visible through the overhead inside rearview mirror begins at the rear bumper and could extend how far behind the bus?
choice_b: 200 feet
choice_c: 300 feet
choice_d: 400 feet or more
explanation: The manual states there is a large blind spot that begins at the rear bumper and could extend up to 400 feet or more behind the bus.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.1.6 Overhead Inside Rearview Mirror

question: What must a school bus driver use to monitor traffic in the area behind the bus that is not visible in the overhead inside mirror?
choice_b: The exterior side mirrors
choice_c: A backup camera
choice_d: A spotter positioned behind the bus
explanation: Because of the large blind spot behind the bus, the driver must use the exterior side mirrors to monitor traffic that approaches and enters this area.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.1.6 Overhead Inside Rearview Mirror

question: According to the manual, students are more likely to be killed in which circumstance?
choice_a: While waiting inside the school building
choice_b: While riding inside the school bus as passengers
choice_c: While riding a bicycle to school
choice_d: While getting on or off the school bus
explanation: The manual states that more students are killed while getting on or off a school bus each year than are killed as passengers inside a school bus.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2 Loading and Unloading

question: Can a school bus driver change the location of an official school bus stop on their own judgment?
choice_a: Yes, at any time the driver believes it is safer
choice_b: Yes, but only during bad weather
choice_c: No, never without written approval from the appropriate school district official
choice_d: Yes, if a parent requests it
explanation: The manual states a driver should never change the location of a bus stop without written approval from the appropriate school district official.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.1 Approaching the Stop

question: When approaching a school bus stop, about how far (or how many seconds) before the stop should alternating flashing amber warning lights generally be activated?
choice_a: At least 500 feet or approximately 30 seconds
choice_b: At least 50 feet or 1-2 seconds
choice_c: Only after the bus has come to a complete stop
choice_d: At least 200 feet or approximately 5-10 seconds
explanation: The manual states amber warning lights should be activated at least 200 feet, or approximately 5-10 seconds, before the school bus stop, or in accordance with state law.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.1 Approaching the Stop

question: About how far (or how many seconds) before pulling over should the right turn signal be activated when approaching a school bus stop?
choice_b: 100-300 feet or approximately 3-5 seconds
choice_c: 1,000 feet or about 20 seconds
choice_d: There is no recommended distance
explanation: The manual states the driver should turn on the right turn signal about 100-300 feet, or approximately 3-5 seconds, before pulling over.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.1 Approaching the Stop

question: When stopping at a designated bus stop, the front bumper of the bus should come to a full stop how far from the students?
choice_b: At least 25 feet away
choice_c: At least 10 feet away
choice_d: Right next to the students for easy boarding
explanation: The manual states the driver should bring the school bus to a full stop with the front bumper at least 10 feet away from students at the designated stop, forcing students to walk to the bus so the driver has a better view of their movements.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.1 Approaching the Stop

question: What should a school bus driver do with the transmission and parking brake at each bus stop?
choice_a: Turn off the engine completely every time
choice_b: Shift into reverse to warn approaching traffic
choice_c: Place the transmission in Park (or Neutral if there is no Park position) and set the parking brake
choice_d: Leave the transmission in Drive with a foot on the brake
explanation: At each stop, the driver should place the transmission in Park, or in Neutral if there is no Park shift point, and set the parking brake.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.1 Approaching the Stop

question: When students are loading onto the bus in the dark, what should the driver do regarding the dome light?
choice_a: Turn it off so it does not distract other drivers
choice_b: Leave the dome light on
choice_c: Flash the dome light on and off repeatedly
choice_d: The manual does not mention the dome light
explanation: During loading, students should board slowly, in single file, using the handrail, and the dome light should be on while loading in the dark.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.2 Loading Procedures

question: Before moving the bus after students have boarded, the driver should wait until students are:
choice_b: Counted twice by another adult
choice_c: Wearing seatbelts and holding the handrail
choice_d: Seated and facing forward
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to wait until students are seated and facing forward before moving the bus.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.2 Loading Procedures

question: If a school bus driver cannot account for a student outside the bus during loading, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Ask the other students to go search for the missing student
choice_b: Leave immediately to stay on schedule and report it later
choice_c: Secure the bus, take the key, and check around and underneath the bus
choice_d: Call the school district and wait with the engine running
explanation: If a student cannot be accounted for, the driver should secure the bus, take the key, and check around and underneath the bus.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.2 Loading Procedures

question: After unloading along the route, students should walk to a position where they are:
choice_a: At least 10 feet away from the side of the bus, where the driver can plainly see them
choice_b: Anywhere they choose, as quickly as possible
choice_c: Directly behind the rear bumper
choice_d: Immediately in front of the bus, out of mirror view
explanation: Students should be told to exit the bus and walk at least 10 feet away from the side of the bus to a position where the driver can plainly see all students.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.3 Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: If a school bus driver realizes they missed a student's unloading stop, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Immediately back up to the correct stop
choice_b: Radio the student's parents before proceeding
choice_c: Do not back up; follow local procedures
choice_d: Turn around only at the very next intersection
explanation: The manual specifically notes that if you have missed a student's unloading stop, you should not back up and should follow local procedures.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.3 Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: When a student must cross the roadway in front of a stopped school bus, how far in front of the right corner of the bumper should the student walk before stopping at the edge of the roadway?
choice_b: At least 50 feet
choice_c: At least 5 feet
choice_d: At least 10 feet
explanation: Students should walk to a location at least 10 feet in front of the right corner of the bumper, then stop at the right edge of the roadway where the driver can see the student's feet.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.3 Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: When unloading students at school, as opposed to along the route, what additional step should the driver take to secure the bus?
choice_a: Turn off the ignition switch and remove the key if leaving the driver's compartment
choice_b: Immediately drive to the bus lot
choice_c: Nothing different is required
choice_d: Leave the engine running for the heater
explanation: When unloading at school, the driver should secure the bus by turning off the ignition switch and removing the key if leaving the driver's compartment.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.4 Unloading Procedures at School

question: During a school bus post-trip inspection, the driver should walk through and around the bus looking for all of the following EXCEPT:
choice_b: Articles left on the bus
choice_c: The bus's fuel economy rating
choice_d: Sleeping students
explanation: The post-trip inspection looks for articles left on the bus, sleeping students, open windows and doors, mechanical or operational problems, and damage or vandalism, not fuel economy.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.6 Post-trip Inspection

question: Which of the following is listed as a condition requiring a MANDATORY evacuation of a school bus?
choice_b: The bus is running 10 minutes behind schedule
choice_c: The bus is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing
choice_d: The bus has a flat tire in a parking lot
explanation: The driver must evacuate the bus if it is on fire or threatened by fire, is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing, faces imminent collision, or requires evacuation due to a hazardous materials spill.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.3.1 Planning for Emergencies

question: A "safe place" for evacuated students should generally be at least how far off the road, in the direction of oncoming traffic?
choice_b: 100 feet
choice_c: 500 feet
choice_d: 50 feet
explanation: The manual states a safe place will be at least 100 feet off the road in the direction of oncoming traffic, to keep students from being hit by debris if a vehicle collides with the bus.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: If evacuating students due to a hazardous materials spill, the manual recommends leading them upwind of the bus at least how far?
choice_b: 100 feet
choice_c: 50 feet
choice_d: 300 feet
explanation: The manual recommends leading students upwind of the bus at least 300 feet if there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: If a school bus is in the direct path of a sighted tornado and no building shelter is readily available, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Have students stand against the bus for shelter
choice_b: Continue driving away from the tornado at high speed
choice_c: Escort students to a nearby ditch or culvert and have them lie face down with hands covering their heads
choice_d: Keep students on the bus with seatbelts fastened
explanation: If shelter in a building is not available, the driver should escort students to a nearby ditch or culvert, direct them to lie face down with hands covering their heads, and avoid areas subject to flash floods.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: What defines a "passive" railroad-highway crossing?
choice_a: It has flashing red lights and gates
choice_b: It has no traffic control device installed
choice_c: It is only used by freight trains
choice_d: It is monitored remotely by the railroad
explanation: A passive crossing does not have any type of traffic control device; the decision to proceed rests entirely on the driver after searching for a train.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.1 Types of Crossings

question: Active railroad-highway crossings are equipped with which of the following?
choice_b: Pavement markings only
choice_c: Flashing red lights, with or without bells, or flashing red lights with bells and gates
choice_d: Only a yellow round advance warning sign
explanation: Active crossings have a traffic control device such as flashing red lights, with or without bells, or flashing red lights with bells and gates.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.1 Types of Crossings

question: If a white stop line is painted on the pavement before a railroad crossing, where must the front of the school bus remain while stopped?
choice_b: It does not matter as long as the bus is stopped
choice_c: On top of the stop line
choice_d: Past the stop line but before the crossbuck
explanation: The manual states the front of the school bus must remain behind the white stop line while stopped at the crossing.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.2 Warning Signs and Devices

question: What does a crossbuck sign at a railroad crossing require the driver to do?
choice_a: Proceed without stopping if no train is visible
choice_b: Sound the horn continuously while crossing
choice_c: Only slow down, never stop
choice_d: Yield the right-of-way to the train
explanation: The crossbuck sign marks the crossing and requires the driver to yield the right-of-way to the train; if there is no white stop line, the driver must stop before the crossbuck.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.2 Warning Signs and Devices

question: If the gate at a railroad crossing stays down after the train has passed, what should the school bus driver do?
choice_a: Do not drive around the gate; call the dispatcher
choice_b: Back away and take an alternate route without reporting it
choice_c: Wait exactly one minute, then proceed regardless
choice_d: Drive around the gate carefully
explanation: If the gate stays down after the train passes, the manual instructs the driver not to drive around the gate and instead call the dispatcher.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.2 Warning Signs and Devices

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, a school bus driver should activate hazard lights approximately how far before the crossing?
choice_b: 500 feet
choice_c: 50 feet
choice_d: 100 feet
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to activate hazard lights approximately 200 feet before the crossing to make their intentions known.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: When stopping at a railroad crossing, a school bus should stop no closer than 15 feet and no farther than how many feet from the nearest rail?
choice_b: 25 feet
choice_c: 50 feet
choice_d: 75 feet
explanation: The manual states the bus should stop no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail, where the driver has the best view of the tracks.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: At a multiple-track crossing, where should the school bus stop before proceeding?
choice_a: After the last set of tracks
choice_b: Only before the first set of tracks
choice_c: Between each pair of tracks
choice_d: There is no specific stopping point required
explanation: At a multiple-track crossing, the driver should stop only before the first set of tracks, then proceed across all tracks once certain no train is approaching on any track.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: While actually crossing railroad tracks, a school bus driver should:
choice_b: Accelerate rapidly to clear the tracks quickly
choice_c: Cross in a low gear and not change gears while crossing
choice_d: Change to a higher gear for extra power
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to cross the tracks in a low gear and not change gears while crossing.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: If a school bus stalls or becomes trapped on railroad tracks, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Move students to the back of the bus for safety
choice_b: Get everyone out and move away from the bus at an angle that is away from the tracks and toward the direction of the approaching train
choice_c: Try repeatedly to restart the engine before evacuating
choice_d: Stay on the bus and wait for help
explanation: If the bus stalls or is trapped on the tracks, the driver must get everyone out and off the tracks immediately, moving away at an angle that is both away from the tracks and toward the train.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.4 Special Situations

question: To determine an acceptable containment or storage area beyond a railroad crossing, the manual recommends adding how many feet to the length of the school bus?
choice_b: 5 feet
choice_c: 25 feet
choice_d: 10 feet
explanation: As a general rule, the manual recommends adding 15 feet to the length of the school bus to determine an acceptable amount of containment or storage area beyond a crossing.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.4 Special Situations

question: Federal requirements mandate antilock braking systems (ABS) on air-braked buses, trucks, trailers, and converter dollies built on or after what date?
choice_b: March 1, 2002
choice_c: March 1, 1995
choice_d: January 1, 2000
explanation: The Department of Transportation requires ABS on air brake vehicles, including trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies, built on or after March 1, 1998.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.6.1 Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: What color is the ABS malfunction lamp on a school bus's instrument panel?
choice_b: Green
choice_c: Blue
choice_d: Yellow
explanation: The manual states a school bus equipped with ABS will have a yellow ABS malfunction lamp on the instrument panel.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.6.1 Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: According to the manual, when braking in an emergency on a bus equipped with ABS, the driver should:
choice_b: Use only the parking brake
choice_c: Not pump the brakes
choice_d: Shift into neutral before braking
explanation: The manual instructs that in emergency braking, the driver should not pump the brakes on a bus equipped with ABS.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.6.3 Braking with ABS

question: Which statement about ABS is TRUE according to the manual?
choice_a: ABS allows you to safely follow other vehicles more closely
choice_b: ABS eliminates the need for regular brake maintenance
choice_c: ABS will prevent skids caused by spinning the drive wheels
choice_d: ABS will not necessarily shorten stopping distance
explanation: The manual notes ABS helps maintain vehicle control but will not necessarily shorten stopping distance, and it will not prevent skids caused by spinning the drive wheels (power skids) or over-speed in a turn.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.6.5 Safety Reminders

question: Roof-mounted white strobe lights on a school bus should be used when:
choice_b: Crossing any intersection, regardless of visibility
choice_c: Loading students in bright daylight
choice_d: The bus is parked overnight
explanation: The manual states the overhead strobe light should be used when visibility is limited, meaning the driver cannot easily see around the bus.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.7.1 Strobe Lights

question: According to the manual, when should a school bus be backed up?
choice_a: Whenever convenient to save time on the route
choice_b: Backing a school bus is never permitted under any circumstances
choice_c: Only when there is no other safe way to move the vehicle, and never with students outside the bus
choice_d: Anytime a lookout happens to be available
explanation: Backing a school bus is strongly discouraged; the driver should back up only when there is no other safe way to move the vehicle, and should never back up when students are outside the bus.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.7.3 Backing

question: When a school bus driver posts a lookout to assist with backing, what is the lookout's role?
choice_a: To operate the hazard lights from outside the bus
choice_b: To warn the driver about obstacles, approaching persons, and other vehicles, not to give directions
choice_c: To physically direct the exact steering movements of the driver
choice_d: To stand in front of the bus to block traffic
explanation: The purpose of the lookout is to warn the driver about obstacles, approaching persons, and other vehicles; the lookout should not give directions on how to back the bus.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.7.3 Backing

question: A school bus can have a tail swing of up to how many feet?
choice_b: One foot
choice_c: Three feet
choice_d: Two feet
explanation: The manual states a school bus can have up to a three-foot tail swing, so the driver needs to check mirrors before and during turning movements.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.7.4 Tail Swing

question: When handling a serious student behavior problem, which of the following is NOT recommended by the manual?
choice_a: Speak respectfully but firmly to the offender
choice_b: Stop the bus and park in a safe location off the road
choice_c: Request that the student move to a seat near the driver if needed
choice_d: Put the student off the bus at any location the driver chooses along the route
explanation: The manual states a driver should never put a student off the bus except at school or at his or her designated school bus stop.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.5.2 Handling Serious Problems
